title: Highlights from ENGAGE 26: AI-Ready Smart Data Was Center Stage
summary: ENGAGE 26 provided enterprises with updates on NETSCOUT's AI-Ready Smart Data and how new capabilities can take their IT and security initiatives to new heights.
body_markdown:
Although ENGAGE 26 is in the rear-view mirror, attendees came away with valuable insights into NETSCOUT innovations that will help enterprises turn network intelligence into action. In a recent blog leading up to the event, we shared[enterprise observability](https://www.netscout.com/observability) sessions that should not be missed; those sessions explored how organizations can address today’s performance challenges while preparing for the future of AI-driven operations.


Across the four major enterprise observability breakouts, a common theme emerged: The path to more predictive, autonomous operations begins with trusted, AI-ready NETSCOUT Smart Data that delivers the visibility, context, and actionable intelligence necessary to make better decisions.


## Moving Beyond Reactive Troubleshooting


Enterprise IT teams are under tremendous pressure to maintain high-quality performance and availability across hybrid clouds, distributed applications, and increasingly interconnected multivendor networks. Traditional monitoring tools provide important information, but they lack a complete end-to-end picture of what is happening across the digital environment. ENGAGE 26 sessions explored how NETSCOUT’s[nGeniusONE](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngeniusone-solution) and[InfiniStreamNG](https://www.netscout.com/product/isng-platform) solutions help organizations address these challenges via comprehensive network and application observability.


NETSCOUT solutions for observability capture and analyze actual network activity, providing valuable operational insight necessary to accelerate root cause identification, reduce mean time to repair (MTTR), and improve digital experiences. Further, they help IT organizations move beyond reactive problem isolation to anticipating and preventing disruptions with more intelligent operational insights.


## Why AI-Ready Smart Data Matters


An important takeaway from the enterprise sessions was the critical role of data quality and context in successful, comprehensive observability and AI initiatives. Traditional metrics, events, logs, and traces (MELT) remain valuable, but they can miss essential details about actual network behavior, application dependencies, and user experiences.[NETSCOUT Smart Data](https://www.netscout.com/what-is/smart-data) enriches these sources with high-fidelity intelligence derived from observed network and application activity. It captures operational ground truth, revealing the context needed to go beyond the problem to pinpoint what happened, where, and why.


As enterprises introduce AI into their network operations, this context becomes especially important. AI systems depend on reliable, complete information to produce meaningful, actionable insights. NETSCOUT’s AI-ready Smart Data, providing a structured, enriched foundation, helps organizations accelerate troubleshooting efforts, empowers confident decision-making, and ensures operational efficiencies.


## Bringing Smart Data into AI Workflows with Omnis AI Insights


A major innovation highlighted at ENGAGE 26 was NETSCOUT’s[recently announced Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectivity for Omnis AI Insights](https://ir.netscout.com/news/news-details/2026/NETSCOUT-Adds-MCP-Connectivity-Putting-AI-Ready-Smart-Data-Directly-Into-the-Hands-of-AI-Assistants-and-Agents/default.aspx?tblci=GigaOm+Network+Observabilty+Radar) , enabled through[Omnis Sensor](https://www.netscout.com/product/omnis-sensor) and[Omnis Streamer](https://www.netscout.com/product/omnis-streamer) . Omnis Sensor generates contextual network intelligence at the point of observation, while Omnis Streamer curates and delivers Smart Data as datasets known as the Omnis AI Feed to analytics, observability, security, and other operational platforms. Its built-in MCP server provides large-language models (LLMs) and AI agents with on-demand access to relevant network intelligence at runtime.


For enterprises, the value of the Omnis AI Insights solution with MCP is in its more accurate AI-assisted analysis and investigations, faster navigation of fragmented telemetry, and greater flexibility to integrate trusted network intelligence into existing AIOps and automation investments.


## Simplifying Troubleshooting with nGenius Copilot


NETSCOUT also highlighted another recent innovation at ENGAGE 26,[introducing the nGenius Copilot for Enterprise](https://ir.netscout.com/news/news-details/2026/NETSCOUT-Accelerates-Problem-Solving-With-Conversational-AI/default.aspx?tblci=GigaOm+Network+Observabilty+Radar) , an AI-powered conversational extension to[nGeniusONE](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngeniusone-solution) that makes sophisticated observability insights more accessible across IT teams. Using natural-language questions, IT professionals can investigate service disruptions, access supporting Smart Data evidence, explore relevant visualizations, and better assess potential business impact.


[nGenius Copilot](https://www.netscout.com/product/ngenius-copilot) helps experienced engineers investigate problems more efficiently while simultaneously empowering a broader range of IT professionals to gain actionable insights more efficiently by simplifying access to the complex operational intelligence in the nGeniusONE solution.


## Looking Ahead: From Insight to Intelligent Action


The enterprise discussions at ENGAGE 26, in both formal panel sessions and informal conversations with peers, reflected similar conclusions that achieving success with AI adoption in network operations requires more than new tools. It requires trusted data, meaningful operational context, and solutions that fit existing workflows.


The combination of NETSCOUT’s observability solutions, AI-ready Smart Data, Omnis AI Insights, and nGenius Copilot provide the next-level technology innovations needed for enterprises to operate more efficiently today while advancing toward predictive and increasingly autonomous operations in the future. The next era of enterprise observability isn’t just about collecting more data. Rather, it is about delivering the right intelligence, with the right context, to enable fast decisions and strategic business outcomes.
